summary: Psyonix's car-soccer franchise, from the PlayStation 3 predecessor through Rocket League's cross-platform live service, mobile Sideswipe, and Fortnite-integrated Rocket Racing.

entries.title: Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars

emulation.notes: Prefer original PS3 hardware for compatibility; RPCS3 may be used for preservation testing. Online service is not a reliable route.

primary.why: Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars released only for PlayStation 3 in 2008/2009 and is the direct predecessor to Rocket League. PlayStation 3 is the sole release route, although online servers later shut down.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 3 version for local/single-player content; online play should not be assumed after the reported 2023 server shutdown.

all_releases.fidelity: Only release; PS3 vehicular soccer predecessor with local/single-player modes and formerly online multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: primary: sole released platform and complete version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PS3 is the sole release platform.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster; online servers were reported shut down in January 2023, so preservation is local/offline-focused.

entries.title: Rocket League
entries.definitive_edition: Windows current free-to-play build, with PS4/Xbox One/Switch secondary routes for platform-exclusive cosmetics

emulation.notes: Run the active Windows build natively; emulation is not useful for current online play, and platform-exclusive cosmetics depend on platform/account access.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC live-service build at highest stable settings

primary.why: Rocket League released first for PlayStation 4 and Windows in 2015, later adding Xbox One, macOS, Linux, and Nintendo Switch, with macOS/Linux online support ending in 2020 and the game becoming free-to-play in 2020. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible current live-service route, while PlayStation, Xbox, and Switch preserve platform-exclusive vehicle cosmetics.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows PC build through Epic's active distribution path at the highest stable settings; use PS4, Xbox One, and Switch only if preserving their platform-exclusive vehicles/cosmetics matters.

secondary.why: Preserves the PlayStation-exclusive Sweet Tooth vehicle/cosmetic route noted in public platform coverage.
secondary.how_to_play: Use the PS4 version or compatible PlayStation access with an account that has the platform-exclusive item access.

secondary.why: Preserves Xbox-exclusive Warthog and Armadillo vehicle/cosmetic content noted in public platform coverage.
secondary.how_to_play: Use the Xbox version with an account/platform setup that has the Xbox-exclusive vehicle access.

secondary.why: Preserves Nintendo-themed Mario, Luigi, and Metroid-inspired car designs.
secondary.how_to_play: Use the Nintendo Switch version with a Nintendo account/platform setup that can access the exclusive cosmetics.

all_releases.fidelity: Current PC live-service build with highest configurable fidelity and cross-platform play.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most flexible current route.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console launch route with PlayStation-exclusive vehicle/cosmetic content.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserves platform-exclusive content not represented by Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Console port with Xbox-exclusive vehicle/cosmetic content and previous DLC included at launch.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserves platform-exclusive content not represented by Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Mac port whose online services were dropped in March 2020.
all_releases.reason: skip: online support ended and no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Linux port whose online services were dropped in March 2020.
all_releases.reason: skip: online support ended and no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable/console version with Nintendo-themed exclusive car designs and visual compromises versus stronger hardware.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserves Nintendo-exclusive content not represented by Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the best current fidelity/live-service route, but PlayStation, Xbox, and Switch have platform-exclusive vehicle cosmetics that require secondary routes for content preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: macOS and Linux online support ended in 2020; older physical Collector's/updated editions bundled DLC or extra cars, but the current live-service model has changed ownership and availability.

entries.title: Rocket League Sideswipe
entries.definitive_edition: Android or iOS current mobile release; Android as the primary access route

emulation.notes: Use active mobile app distribution where available; general emulation is secondary to real mobile hardware.

primary.why: Rocket League Sideswipe launched worldwide for Android and iOS in late 2021 as a free-to-play 2D mobile spin-off. Android is the most flexible mobile preservation/access route, while iOS remains equivalent for normal play where available.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Android version through the current mobile distribution path if available; use iOS as an equivalent mobile route where the app remains obtainable.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile free-to-play 2D Rocket League spin-off with flexible device access.

all_releases.reason: skip: equivalent mobile route and no sourced content advantage over Android.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced Android/iOS-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service mobile title; season/content availability changes over time.

entries.title: Rocket Racing

emulation.notes: Run through the active Fortnite client on Windows while the mode remains available; emulation is not a preservation route for this live-service mode.

primary.why: Rocket Racing released inside Fortnite on 8 December 2023 across Android, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, but Epic announced the mode will be discontinued in October 2026, making preservation time-limited.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Fortnite on Windows while Rocket Racing remains available; after the announced shutdown, only vehicle cosmetics and creator-tool remnants are expected to persist in other modes/tools.

all_releases.fidelity: Fortnite-based PC release with highest configurable fidelity while the mode remains online.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity route before the announced shutdown.
